title.value: Behind the Machine’s Gaze: Neural Networks with Biologically-inspired Constraints Exhibit Human-like Visual Attention
title.justification: The paper describes the development of the Neural Visual Attention (NeVA) algorithm which uses biologically-inspired constraints to guide neural networks in mimicking human-like visual attention.
title.quote: We propose the Neural Visual Attention (NeVA) algorithm to generate visual scanpaths in a top-down manner.

extractions.description: The paper develops a Neural Visual Attention (NeVA) algorithm that imposes biologically-inspired foveated vision constraints on neural networks, enabling them to create human-like visual scanpaths without explicit training. NeVA leverages task-driven cues to guide the attention mechanism, aiming to simulate human visual attention dynamics. The algorithm is evaluated on its performance in replicating human scanpaths and its applicability in resource-constrained scenarios.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving computational models of visual attention to mimic human behaviors rather than directly addressing issues related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We propose the Neural Visual Attention (NeVA) algorithm to generate visual scanpaths in a top-down manner.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper does not align with any Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category. It is primarily concerned with human visual attention modeling through biologically-inspired neural networks.
primary_category.quote: Our goal is not to develop a biologically plausible model of human attention but rather to observe whether imposing biologically-inspired constraints on neural networks will lead to more human-like image explorations.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit any specific sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, focusing instead on neural network models and visual attention.
primary_sub_category.quote: The vast majority of studies have focused on improving saliency map estimation.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not propose or address a new category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: Our contributions can be summarized as follows: We use common metrics to measure similarity between simulated and human scanpaths, and introduce and motivate the String-Based Time-Delay Embeddings (SBTDE), an alternative metric to account for stochastic components in human behavior.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not suggest a new sub-category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as its focus is on computational visual attention modeling.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In an extensive evaluation with multiple well-established eye-tracking datasets, we show that scanpaths generated by NeVA exhibit the highest similarity to humans compared to state-of-the-art unsupervised methods, as measured by several metrics.
